entries.description: Security baseline standard shared by code writers and reviewers, with the severities reviewers use: no secrets in code, fail-fast env validation, parameterized queries, input validation at boundaries, dependency hygiene. Use when writing or reviewing code that handles user input, credentials, or external data.

Async patterns standard shared by code writers and reviewers, with the severities reviewers use: independent awaits run in parallel, a timeout on every external call, bounded fan-out, no event-loop blocking. Use when writing or reviewing async/await code, parallel operations, or queue consumers.

Concurrency standard for the CLI and for several sessions sharing one checkout, shared by code writers and reviewers, with the severities reviewers use: a lock file is taken by exclusive create, files are written via temp file and rename, one write per JSONL record, child-process fan-out is bounded, child output is capped. Use when writing or reviewing code that touches shared state files, lock files, JSONL logs or spawned child processes.

keryx CLI decisions: exit codes (0 clean, 1 found something, 2 cannot tell), machine-readable output on stdout and diagnostics on stderr, versioned --json shapes, unknown flags refused, and flags renamed by alias with one notice or removed by refusing them by name. Use when adding, changing, or retiring a command, subcommand, flag, or --json payload that people already run.
